step1_analysis.description: A broadband transimpedance amplifier designed to convert high-speed input current from a photodetector into an output voltage. It utilizes a Cherry-Hooper or similar broadband architecture with feedback to achieve high bandwidth for 40 Gb/s optical communication systems.

paper_reference.title: SiGe Differential Transimpedance Amplifier With 50-GHz Bandwidth

Transimpedance_Gain.description: The ratio of the output voltage to the input current, expressed in dB ohms.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain is primarily determined by the feedback resistors (RFB1, RFB2). 20 * log10(280 ohms) ≈ 49 dB. With SKY130 generic MOSFETs or default BJTs, open-loop gain might be lower, slightly reducing closed-loop gain.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Feedback sets the gain, so it remains relatively constant across technologies as long as the open-loop gain is sufficient.

Bandwidth_3dB.description: The frequency at which the transimpedance gain drops by 3 dB from its midband value.

sky130_expected.calculation: Bandwidth is limited by the fT of the technology. SKY130 NMOS fT is ~30-40 GHz. Closed-loop TIA bandwidth is typically a fraction of fT depending on the transimpedance limit.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 130nm CMOS is significantly slower than the 200-GHz SiGe HBTs used in the original paper, so the bandwidth will scale down proportionally.

Power_Consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the amplifier from the supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. Using a 1.8V supply instead of 5.2V, and assuming similar bias currents (e.g., 20-30 mA total).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The lower supply voltage of SKY130 (1.8V vs 5.2V) will drastically reduce the total power consumption compared to the paper.

Input_Referred_Noise.description: The equivalent noise current at the input that would produce the observed output noise.

sky130_expected.calculation: Dominated by the thermal noise of the feedback resistor (4kT/R_fb) and the input transistor channel noise.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Noise performance will be slightly worse in CMOS due to lower gm/Id and higher flicker noise, though thermal noise from the feedback resistor remains constant.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure transimpedance gain, -3dB bandwidth, power consumption, and input-referred noise. Missing resistor values are parameterized to allow simulation.
step3_testbench.spice:
* SiGe Differential TIA Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameterized missing resistor values
.param R_default=1k
.param R_fb=280
.param R_out=50

* DUT Netlist
R1 GND IN {R_default}
Q1 GND N2 N7 npn
Q2 N3 N3 N17 npn
Q3 N2 N2 N10 npn
Q4 IN N0 N11 npn
Q5 N8 IN N19 npn
R2 N7 N12 {R_default}
Q6 OUT N7 N20 npn
R3 N11 N12 {R_default}
R4 GND OUT {R_out}
R5 N1 N12 {R_default}
R6 N10 N12 {R_default}
Q7 N19 N0 N15 npn
Q8 N14 IN N0 npn
Q9 N9 N0 N13 npn
Q10 N18 N18 N14 npn
R7 N12 N15 {R_default}
R8 N12 N17 {R_default}
RL2 N4 GND {R_default}
R10 N12 N13 {R_default}
RE1 N9 N9 {R_default}
RL1 GND N8 {R_default}
Q11 N4 IN N19 npn
RE2 N9 N20 {R_default}
RFB2 N2 IN {R_fb}
R15 GND OUT {R_out}
RFB1 N3 IN {R_fb}
Q12 GND N4 N2 npn
Q13 GND GND N18 npn
Q14 OUT N1 LABEL_NET_0 npn
Q15 N3 N8 GND pnp
Q16 N1 N3 GND pnp

* Generic BJT models for simulation
.model npn npn bf=100 is=1e-15
.model pnp pnp bf=50 is=1e-15

* Supplies and Stimulus
* GND is treated as the positive supply (0V), N12 as the negative supply (-1.8V)
VEE N12 0 DC -1.8
VLABEL LABEL_NET_0 0 DC -1.8
IIN IN 0 DC 0 AC 1

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(VEE) * 1.8
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 50 10M 100G
let gain_db = vdb(OUT)
meas ac midband_gain find gain_db at=100M
let gain_3db = midband_gain - 3
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=gain_3db fall=1

* 3. Noise Analysis
noise v(OUT) IIN dec 10 100M 10G
setplot noise1
print inoise_spectrum

quit
.endc
